exercises.title: A min-heap in a slice
exercises.task: Read MinHeap. up and down are the same as in Go's container/heap (hover heap. names in the editor to compare). Run pushes numbers and prints the slice as a tree, then pops them: they come out smallest first.

exercises.title: Write up and down
exercises.task: Push and Pop are given. Fill up (a new value climbs while it is smaller than its parent) and down (the root sinks, swapping with its smaller child, while a child is smaller).
hints: Parent of i: (i-1)/2. Children of i: 2*i+1 and 2*i+2.
up: for i > 0: if h[i] < h[parent], swap and continue from the parent; otherwise stop.
down: find the smaller of the existing children (check left < len(h) and right < len(h)); if it is smaller than h[i], swap and continue from it; otherwise stop.

exercises.title: The k most frequent words
exercises.task: From a count per word, return the k most frequent words (ties: alphabetical order). Use container/heap with a min-heap of at most k entries: when it grows past k, pop the smallest. That is O(n log k) instead of sorting all n.
hints: A type type minH []item with Len, Less, Swap, Push(x any), Pop() any: the five methods of heap.Interface.
"Smallest" here means the one to drop first: fewer counts, and on equal counts the name that comes later alphabetically.
At the end the heap holds the top k, smallest on top: pop them all into a slice, then reverse it.
